To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new driver is proposed for a synchronous buck VR, which can achieve significant switching loss reduction, gate energy recovery, and reduced conduction and reverse recovery losses of the body diodes; the new driver can drive two switches independently with different drive current to achieve the optimal design of the driver, control, and synchronous-rectifier switches; and the improved driver using integrated magnetic cores is presented for multiphase VRs to reduce the number magnetic cores and the associated core losses.
a new current source gate driver is proposed to reduce switching losses, conduction losses, body diode losses and reverse recovery losses.
a new gate drive circuit for the synchronous buck converter has been proposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a high-efficiency, low-voltage buck VR for a 12-V battery-powered portable system.
the design of a 12-V 1-MHz high-efficiency synchronous-buck voltage regulator.
the following issues: (1) the new current-source gate driver for the synchronous buck converter; and (2) multiphase buck VRs using the new driver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work presents a new driver for a synchronous buck regulator that improves efficiency and power density significantly.
the new driver approach can achieve a significant efficiency improvement in the 1-MHz buck VR.
a 1-MHz 12-V synchronous buck voltage regulator using the new driver has achieved 87.3%-efficiency at 20-A load and 82.8%-efficiency at a 30-A load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new driver approach can achieve a 1-MHz 12-V 1.5-30-A buck VR with an efficiency of over 80% at 30 A and over 90% at 1.5 A.
we proposed a new current-source driver to improve the performance of the buck VR.

we have developed a new current-source driver for the control MOSFETS and the synchronous-rectifiers, which can achieve: 3.5-5.6% efficiency improvement for a single-phase buck regulator; 4.2-6.5% efficiency improvement for two-phase buck regulators; 6.1-8.2% efficiency improvement for three-phase buck regulators; and 7.2-9.3% efficiency improvement for four-phase buck regulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed driver approach is attractive for high-efficiency VRs.
the driver circuit is a critical component for improving the overall efficiency.
the proposed driver can be applied in a wide range of applications, such as high-voltage VRs and power factor correction (PFC) converters.
